title: Competitive exclusion in the two-type contact process with unequal death rates
statement: In the two-species competition model (a multitype contact process with birth rates beta_i and death rates delta_i), show that species 1 outcompetes species 2 when the two dispersal distributions are the same and beta_1/delta_1 > beta_2/delta_2. Durrett notes that this is what the Competitive Exclusion Principle predicts and that simulation supports it.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on competitive exclusion for the multitype contact process. Neuhauser's 1992 ergodic theorems for the multitype contact process remain the standing result and cover equal death rates; Cox-Durrett-Perkins (Asterisque 340, 2011) and Durrett's 'Spatial evolutionary games with small selection coefficients' (EJP 2014) cover perturbations of the VOTER model, i.e. a small-selection regime, which is a different hypothesis from the source's beta_1/delta_1 > beta_2/delta_2 with no smallness assumption. No paper found that proves the stated exclusion for unequal death rates. Kept open.

attempt.method: Locate the exact place where the equal-death-rate proof breaks. Neuhauser's argument for equal delta uses the multitype duality: the two types share one graphical construction, and the ancestral process of a site is a single coalescing branching random walk whose type is decided by the initial condition it reaches, so the competition is settled by a single comparison of birth rates.
attempt.result: With delta_1 different from delta_2 that duality is destroyed, and not for a technical reason: a type-i particle dies at rate delta_i, so the ancestral lineage of a site would have to know its own type in order to run its death clock. The dual is therefore a TYPE-DEPENDENT branching-coalescing walk, and the type is exactly what one is trying to determine - the duality is circular. The quantity beta_i/delta_i is the mean-field invasion fitness (the mean-field equilibrium density of type i alone is 1 - delta_i/beta_i, increasing in beta_i/delta_i), so the conjecture says the spatial model respects the mean-field ordering. That is not automatic: the spatial critical value of the one-type contact process is beta/delta > lambda_c > 1, so the spatial fitness ordering could in principle differ from the mean-field one; what saves the conjecture, if it is true, is that both types feel the SAME lattice, so the map (beta, delta) -> spatial invasion speed should be monotone in beta/delta by a scaling of time. This scaling observation is the natural first step and it is not in the source; it does not prove the conjecture because time scaling does not act on the two types simultaneously.
attempt.obstruction: The two-type system with unequal death rates is not attractive in the coordinatewise order that makes type 1 grow at the expense of type 2 (increasing type 1 both helps type 1 and, by occupying sites, hurts type 2 - the standard order works only when the death rates agree so that vacancies are exchangeable). Without attractiveness there is no monotone coupling, without duality there is no ancestral computation, and the block construction gives coexistence results but not exclusion results, because exclusion is an upper bound on one type and the block construction only produces lower bounds.
attempt.key_identity: The mean-field one-type equilibrium is 1 - delta_i/beta_i, so beta_1/delta_1 > beta_2/delta_2 is exactly the statement that type 1 has the larger mean-field carrying capacity; the spatial claim is that a single lattice preserves that ordering.

title: A general coexistence theorem for long-range interactions to replace fast stirring
statement: Durrett's Theorem 5 gives coexistence in a stochastic spatial model with fast stirring at rate eps^{-2} whenever there is a function phi that (i) decreases along solutions of the mean-field ODE, (ii) is convex, and (iii) tends to infinity as min_i u_i tends to 0. Formulate and prove a similar general result for systems with LONG-RANGE interactions, where at present the coexistence proofs are done case by case.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 for a general long-range analogue of the fast-stirring coexistence theorem. Found the case-by-case long-range results the source cites (Durrett-Neuhauser 1997, Durrett-Lanchier 2008) and the later voter-perturbation programme of Cox-Durrett-Perkins, which is a different limit (weak selection around the voter model, not long range with a fixed nonlinearity). No general long-range theorem with a Lyapunov hypothesis of the source's form was found. Kept open.

attempt.method: Carry the proof of Theorem 5 through with the diffusive limit replaced by the nonlocal limit. Under long-range interaction of range N, the hydrodynamic object is not u_t = Laplacian u + f(u) but the nonlocal equation u_t = J*u - u + f(u), where J is the normalised interaction kernel.
attempt.result: The Lyapunov step survives, and the hypothesis that survives it is exactly the one the source already assumes. Set h = phi(u) with phi convex. Jensen's inequality applied to the probability kernel J gives phi(J*u) <= J*phi(u), i.e. phi(J*u) - phi(u) <= (J*h - h). Combining with dphi/dt along the ODE, the same computation that produced dh/dt <= Laplacian h + phi'(u).f(u) in the diffusive case yields dh/dt <= J*h - h + phi'(u).f(u) in the nonlocal case, and the right-hand side is again 'nonlocal heat flow with killing' since phi'(u).f(u) <= 0 by hypothesis (i). So convexity of phi, which in the fast-stirring proof was used against the Laplacian, is precisely the hypothesis that makes the nonlocal generator work, and no new hypothesis on phi is needed. What this does NOT do: it gives the differential inequality, not the coexistence theorem, because the block construction still needs a spreading statement for the nonlocal equation.
attempt.obstruction: The spreading step is where long range and fast stirring genuinely differ. For the diffusive equation, 'one pile makes two piles' follows from a finite-speed travelling front. For the nonlocal equation the front speed is finite only when J has exponential tails; for heavy-tailed J the fronts accelerate and the block construction's fixed space-time box has no analogue. Moreover the long-range particle system does not converge to the nonlocal PDE with a small parameter multiplying the noise the way fast stirring does: as the range N grows the fluctuation term is of order N^{-d/2} and the error in the hydrodynamic approximation must be beaten uniformly over the block, which is exactly what the case-by-case proofs do by hand.
attempt.key_identity: For convex phi and a probability kernel J, Jensen gives phi(J*u) <= J*phi(u); hence the fast-stirring Lyapunov inequality dh/dt <= Laplacian h + phi'(u).f(u) becomes dh/dt <= J*h - h + phi'(u).f(u) with no extra hypothesis.

title: Absence of coexistence in the host-pathogen model when the pathogen is a mutualist
statement: In the three-state host-pathogen model of Durrett and Lanchier, show that coexistence is not possible when lambda_2 < lambda_3 < lambda_1. Durrett explains that in this regime the pathogen is a mutualist (it decreases the rate at which the species is replaced), that starting from 1s and 2s in equilibrium with a small density of 3s the fraction of 2s shrinks and the 3s gain an even bigger advantage, and that in this case there is no interior fixed point.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 for host-pathogen multitype contact process coexistence results after 2009, including the Lanchier-Neuhauser line of work. Found later host-pathogen and multitype papers but none proving the stated non-coexistence for lambda_2 < lambda_3 < lambda_1. Kept open.

attempt.method: Ask what kind of statement 'no coexistence' is, and which of the two standard machines can produce it. Coexistence is a lower bound on both densities and is produced by the block construction; non-coexistence is an upper bound on one density and is produced either by a monotone coupling with a subcritical process or by a Lyapunov/entropy argument on the whole configuration.
attempt.result: The absence of an interior fixed point in the mean-field ODE, which the source records, is not by itself an obstruction to spatial coexistence, and it is important not to read it as one: spatial models routinely coexist where the ODE does not (the catalyst example in the same survey, and cyclic systems, are exactly of that kind). So the mean-field computation cannot be the proof. The route that has content is the invasion argument the source sketches, made into a comparison: if the 3s invade a 1-2 equilibrium and their advantage is monotone increasing in their own density, the density of 3s dominates a supercritical growth process and the 2s are dominated by a subcritical one. The needed structure is monotonicity of the 2s' effective death rate in the density of 3s, which holds exactly in the mutualist ordering lambda_2 < lambda_3 < lambda_1 - and that is the reason the ordering appears in the conjecture.
attempt.obstruction: The comparison requires a monotone coupling of a three-type system, and three-type contact processes are not attractive in any order that keeps both comparisons simultaneously: making the 3s more numerous helps the 3s and hurts the 2s, but it also changes the environment the 1s see, and there is no partial order on {1,2,3} that is preserved by the dynamics. The absence of an interior fixed point is a mean-field fact and does not survive the spatial fluctuation, so the mean-field computation is a heuristic and not an ingredient of a proof.
attempt.key_identity: No interior mean-field fixed point does not imply no spatial coexistence: the catalyst model in the same survey coexists in a parameter range that the source's own mean-field analysis does not predict.

title: Uniqueness of the nontrivial stationary distribution for the sexual reproduction model with fast stirring
statement: Consider the sexual reproduction model with lambda > 4.5. Show that when the stirring rate eps^{-2} is large there is a unique nontrivial stationary distribution. Durrett notes that existence results for stationary distributions are common but convergence results such as the grass-bushes-trees theorem are rare, and that one should start with a concrete case.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on complete convergence theorems for non-attractive spatial models with fast stirring, and on the sexual reproduction (Durrett-Neuhauser) model. Found the existence results and the fast-stirring critical value lambda_c -> 4.5 (Durrett-Neuhauser 1994) but no uniqueness or complete convergence theorem for lambda > 4.5. Kept open.

attempt.method: Ask what a uniqueness proof would have to supply beyond what the block construction already gives, by pushing the block construction as far as it goes.
attempt.result: The block construction gives a two-sided density bound: any stationary distribution nu that is not the all-empty state dominates the upper invariant measure of a supercritical oriented percolation, so nu-a.s. the density is at least some rho_- > 0, and by the same comparison run downwards the density is at most rho_+ < 1, with rho_+ - rho_- tending to 0 as eps -> 0 because both are read off the same PDE steady state. So all nontrivial stationary distributions have the SAME asymptotic density as eps -> 0. That is the honest reach of the standard machinery, and it is strictly weaker than uniqueness: equality of one-dimensional marginals does not determine a measure on {0,1}^{Z^d}. Recording that gap explicitly is the useful output, because it says a proof must add a coupling or a duality, not a sharper density estimate.
attempt.obstruction: Uniqueness for interacting particle systems is proved either by attractiveness plus a complete convergence theorem, or by duality. The sexual reproduction model is not attractive (birth requires TWO occupied neighbours, so adding particles can destroy the pair structure that a competing configuration relied on), and its nonlinearity is quadratic, so there is no dual. Fast stirring supplies a small parameter for the hydrodynamic limit, but the hydrodynamic limit is deterministic and cannot distinguish two stationary laws with the same density: the uniqueness question lives entirely in the fluctuation field, which the eps -> 0 limit erases.
attempt.key_identity: Two-sided block bounds pin the density of every nontrivial stationary law to an interval shrinking with eps, but equality of densities is not equality of laws - the missing ingredient is a coupling, not a better estimate.

title: An explicit coexistence window for the catalyst model without stirring
statement: In the catalyst model (states 0 = vacant, 1 = CO, 2 = O; 0 -> 1 at rate p, a pair of neighbouring 0s -> 22 at rate q/4, adjacent 12 -> 00 at rate r/4), find 0 < p_1 < p_2 < 1 so that coexistence occurs for p in (p_1, p_2). Durrett notes that Bramson and Neuhauser proved coexistence when the O_2s are replaced by an N x N polymer with N large, and that Durrett and Swindle proved coexistence in the original model by introducing fast stirring; simulations suggest the O density drops to 0 discontinuously at the upper critical value.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on the catalyst / CO oxidation (ZGB-type) lattice model and rigorous coexistence without stirring. The Durrett-Swindle fast-stirring result and the Bramson-Neuhauser large-polymer result remain the rigorous statements; nothing found that removes the small parameter. Kept open.

attempt.method: Ask what the small parameter is doing in each of the two existing proofs and whether either can be made quantitative at a fixed lattice.
attempt.result: Both existing proofs buy the same thing: they make the local dynamics close to a deterministic system whose interior fixed point is attracting, so that a single block can be shown to seed its neighbours. Fast stirring does it by a hydrodynamic limit, the N x N polymer by making the vacancy requirement macroscopic. At fixed p, q, r and no stirring there is no small parameter at all, and the only remaining route is a finite-range comparison: exhibit a finite space-time box and a finite set of configurations such that a rigorous estimate on that box (in principle a computer-assisted one, as has been done for other two-dimensional particle systems) shows the block construction's percolation is supercritical. The conjecture's specific shape - an INTERVAL (p_1, p_2) rather than a half-line - is forced by the mean-field structure: the interior fixed point exists only when p < q, and it disappears as p decreases too, so coexistence must be lost at both ends.
attempt.obstruction: The block construction needs 'one occupied block makes two', which for a three-state non-attractive system means controlling a two-dimensional density vector, so the finite-box estimate is over a set of configurations rather than a single event, and its probability must be bounded below explicitly. The discontinuity that simulations report at the upper critical value makes matters worse: near p_2 the block estimate degrades as a first-order transition, so no continuity or perturbative argument can reach the edge of the interval, and any proof will produce an interval strictly inside the true one.
attempt.key_identity: The mean-field interior fixed point exists only for p < q and disappears again as p decreases, which is why the conjectured coexistence region is a bounded interval and not a half-line.

title: Absence of coexistence in the two-type colicin model with equal death rates
statement: In the colicin model of Durrett and Levin (type 1 produces colicin, which raises the death rate of type 2 by an amount proportional to the local density of 1s), show that coexistence is not possible when lambda_1 < lambda_2 and delta_1 = delta_2 = 1. Durrett notes that in the parameter range where the mean-field ODE has an interior fixed point that fixed point is unstable, and that simulations show segregation with the interface moving in favour of the 1s.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on the colicin / allelopathy spatial competition model and rigorous non-coexistence results. Found the Durrett-Levin (1997) analysis and the later interface literature but no proof of non-coexistence under the stated hypotheses. Kept open.

attempt.method: Take the source's own simulation observation seriously and ask what statement it is evidence for: the two types segregate into large single-type regions and the interface moves. That is an interface problem, not a density problem.
attempt.result: Under segregation the long-time behaviour is decided by the sign of the interface velocity, which in the mean-field PDE is the sign of the integral of the reaction term across the connecting orbit - the same computation the source performs for the sexual reproduction model, where c has the sign of the integral of g over the interval between the two stable states. So the conjecture is equivalent to: for lambda_1 < lambda_2 and delta_1 = delta_2 = 1 the corresponding integral is strictly positive, i.e. the colicin advantage always beats the birth-rate disadvantage. This is a scalar computation for the PDE, and it is exactly the content of the mean-field bistability the source reports. What is NOT thereby proved: that the particle system with no stirring segregates at all, or that its interface follows the PDE velocity; those are the two hard steps, and they are what makes the conjecture a conjecture.
attempt.obstruction: The reduction to an interface velocity is rigorous only under fast stirring, where the particle system converges to the PDE. Without a small parameter the interface is rough, its width is of the same order as the lattice spacing, and there is no known way to define its velocity, let alone compare it with the PDE's. The system is also not attractive, so the interface cannot be handled by a monotone comparison with a one-dimensional growth process.
attempt.key_identity: For a bistable reaction term g the travelling-wave speed satisfies c times the integral of (w')^2 equals the integral of g between the two stable states, so the sign of the speed is the sign of that integral - the whole conjecture is that this sign is positive when lambda_1 < lambda_2 and the death rates are equal.

title: Coexistence in the cyclic case of Silvertown's five-species competition model
statement: Show that coexistence always occurs in the cyclic case of Silvertown's model - the multitype biased voter model on five species with the empirically measured invasion matrix alpha_ij given in the survey, in which i replaces j at rate alpha_ij. Durrett adds: 'For partial credit show that coexistence can occur for some parameters', and remarks that a proof by simulation is given in his Figure 9.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on cyclic multitype biased voter models and rigorous coexistence for more than three species. The three-species rock-paper-scissors and cyclic particle system results (Durrett-Griffeath and successors) are the standing rigorous statements; no five-species result with a general invasion matrix was found. Kept open.

attempt.method: Ask what the word 'cyclic' has to mean here for the known three-species proofs to have any chance of transferring, since Silvertown's matrix is a general nonnegative matrix rather than a cyclic permutation.
attempt.result: The three-species proofs use an exact structure that the five-species matrix does not have: for the strictly cyclic system the mean-field replicator dynamics has the conserved quantity prod_i u_i^{c_i} for suitable positive c_i, which is what keeps the interior orbits from spiralling out, and the spatial proof then shows that local spirals stabilise the conserved quantity. For a general tournament matrix such a conserved quantity exists only if the matrix is (after scaling) skew-symmetric on the interior, which is a codimension-positive condition on the 20 entries and is NOT satisfied by Silvertown's measured numbers. So the honest statement is that the conjecture as posed is not the five-species case of the known three-species theorem; it is a different problem, and the 'partial credit' version - coexistence for SOME parameters - is the one for which the conserved-quantity route is available, namely for matrices close to skew-symmetric.
attempt.obstruction: Multitype systems with q > 3 types have no monotone structure and no duality (the biased voter model with unequal rates is not the voter model, so the coalescing-random-walk dual is lost), and the block construction requires a spreading statement for a five-dimensional reaction-diffusion system whose interior fixed point, for the measured matrix, is a spiral rather than a sink. Spreading for a spiral fixed point is not covered by any general theorem.
attempt.key_identity: The replicator dynamics of a skew-symmetric (zero-sum) invasion matrix conserves prod_i u_i^{c_i}, which is what confines the interior orbits; a general measured tournament matrix has no such invariant, so the five-species problem is not the three-species theorem with more indices.

title: Coexistence in the three-species colicin model
statement: Show that coexistence can occur in the three-species colicin model, whose mean-field ODE and simulation are given in the survey's Figures 10 and 11.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on three-strain colicin / rock-paper-scissors bacterial competition and rigorous coexistence. The rigorous literature covers the three-species cyclic particle systems and the Kerr-Riley-Feldman-Bohannan style models at the simulation level; no proof for the survey's three-species colicin model was found. Kept open.

attempt.method: Identify which of the two available coexistence machines applies: the fast-stirring Lyapunov theorem (Theorem 5 of the survey) or the cyclic-structure argument.
attempt.result: The three-species colicin system is a genuine rock-paper-scissors: the colicin producer beats the sensitive strain, the sensitive strain outgrows the resistant one, and the resistant strain outgrows the producer, because producing colicin is costly. That is the structure under which the cyclic machinery could apply, and it is a better target than the five-species problem E0013. Concretely, the fast-stirring theorem needs a convex phi decreasing along the ODE and blowing up at the boundary; for a zero-sum-like three-species replicator the function phi(u) = -sum c_i log u_i is exactly of that type (it blows up at the boundary and is convex), and it is constant, hence nonincreasing, along the ODE when the interaction is skew-symmetric. So for the skew-symmetric idealisation the survey's own Theorem 5 applies and gives coexistence with fast stirring. The genuine colicin matrix is only approximately skew-symmetric because of the cost of production; the honest conclusion is that Theorem 5 applies to a perturbation only if phi remains nonincreasing, which requires the cost term to have the right sign, and that is a checkable inequality on the model's rates rather than a theorem.
attempt.obstruction: Whether the required inequality holds for the actual colicin rates is not settled by the survey, and 'coexistence with fast stirring' is weaker than the question, which is posed for the model as given. Removing the stirring runs into the same wall as E0011: no small parameter, and a three-dimensional density vector to control in the block construction.
attempt.key_identity: phi(u) = -sum_i c_i log u_i is convex and blows up on the boundary of the simplex, and is conserved by a zero-sum replicator flow; it is therefore the natural candidate for the survey's own Theorem 5, and the whole question is whether the colicin production cost keeps it nonincreasing.

title: Coexistence in the spatial Prisoner's Dilemma
statement: Show that coexistence can occur in the spatial Prisoner's Dilemma, i.e. in the Hawks-Doves spatial birth-and-death system with game matrix a = -0.6, b = 0.9, c = -0.9, d = 0.7, whose homogeneously-mixing ODE has the Hawk-to-Dove ratio increasing until the population crashes to 0. Durrett reports that simulations suggest Hawks and Doves coexist in the spatial model, because the ODE dynamics happen locally and Doves left behind recolonise space after a local Hawk crash.
status_search: WebSearch 2026-09-08 on rigorous coexistence in spatial evolutionary games. Cox-Durrett-Perkins, 'Voter model perturbations and reaction diffusion equations' (Asterisque 340, 2011) and Durrett, 'Spatial evolutionary games with small selection coefficients' (EJP 2014, arXiv:1406.5876) determine phase diagrams for spatial games INCLUDING Prisoner's Dilemma cases, but under the hypothesis that the selection coefficient is small (the dynamics is a perturbation of the voter model). Comparing the objects by name: the source's Problem 9 names the Hawks-Doves birth-and-death system with the fixed matrix (-0.6, 0.9, -0.9, 0.7) and no smallness hypothesis, whereas the 2011/2014 theorems name voter-model perturbations with a small selection parameter. Different hypotheses, so the row is kept ADMITTED, with the small-selection results recorded as the closest known relative and the obvious first thing to try.

attempt.method: Ask what the spatial model has that the ODE does not, in a form that could be turned into a proof, and check the mechanism the source proposes: local crashes followed by recolonisation.
attempt.result: The proposed mechanism is a rescue effect and it has a precise signature: the survival of Doves is a statement about the SURVIVAL OF A SUPERCRITICAL GROWTH PROCESS IN THE DEBRIS OF A CRASH, not about a stationary density. That distinguishes this problem from all the others in the survey, and it explains why the mean-field picture (total extinction) is not merely quantitatively wrong but qualitatively so: the ODE has no state in which one region is empty while another is full, and it is exactly such states that carry the coexistence. The route with content is therefore a two-scale block construction in which the block event is 'a block that is mostly Dove at time 0 produces two mostly-Dove blocks at time T even though Hawks invade and crash inside it'. The small-selection theorems of Cox-Durrett-Perkins reach a nearby statement by a different route (perturbation of the voter model), and the natural first step is to check whether the specific matrix (-0.6, 0.9, -0.9, 0.7) can be reached from the voter model by a path of games along which their phase-diagram criterion stays on the coexistence side.
attempt.obstruction: The selection here is not small: the payoff entries are order one, so the process is not a voter-model perturbation and the Cox-Durrett-Perkins rescaling does not apply. Without that rescaling the block event has to be verified for a non-attractive two-type system at fixed parameters, which is the same finite-box obstacle as in E0011. The population can also die out globally, so the block construction must be run for a process that is not conservative, and the usual comparison with oriented percolation requires a lower bound on the total mass that no monotonicity supplies.
attempt.key_identity: Coexistence here is a rescue effect: the invariant object is not a stationary density but the survival of Doves in the wake of local Hawk crashes, a state the homogeneously-mixing ODE cannot represent at all.
